neighbours.label: a passive participle that demands a complement, right after be/get: 'is regarded [as]', 'was ordered [to]', 'was diagnosed [with]', 'is believed [to]'; also 'in the process [of]'. Active uses of the same verbs stay quiet.
fire: Among local historians the mill is regarded as the town's oldest surviving structure.
Two years ago my uncle was diagnosed with a rare blood disorder.
The guards were ordered to search every wagon leaving the camp.
The comet is believed to return once every seventy years.
In her home country the novelist is hailed as a national treasure.
The package was supposed to arrive before the weekend.
Visitors are not allowed to feed the animals in the enclosure.
The museum is in the process of moving its archive to a new wing.
quiet: Local historians regarded the mill with a mixture of pride and worry.
The vet diagnosed the infection quickly and prescribed drops.
The captain ordered fresh supplies and a new map of the coast.
Many villagers believed the old story about the comet.
The crowd hailed a taxi after the concert ended.
The package arrived before the weekend and was opened at once.
The animals in the enclosure were fed and watered at noon.
The museum moved its archive to a new wing last spring.

notes: Card: ' regarded', ' diagnosed', ' hailed', ' ordered', ' supposed', ' process'. Probes: passive uses read 0.47-0.78, active uses of the same verbs and a complement-less passive ('was broken') about 0.01. 'known for' (0.12) and 'considered' (0.08) read low, so the set of verbs is narrower than the label's wording may suggest. The - pole fires on the following preposition ('invited to'), the other half of the same construction.
